stories.body: The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs on 14 economies following an investigation into alleged excess industrial production. China faces a proposed rate of 20%, potentially bringing combined duties on some goods to 45%. Brazil rejected proposed duties on sugar and aircraft and left open the possibility of retaliation, while the EU disputed the justification and called on Washington to honor their trade agreement. The measures remain subject to consultation, with a January 25 hearing suggesting implementation in February or March. A separate US-China trade truce expires January 10.
stories.headline: US proposes tariffs of up to 20% on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU

stories.body: A Houthi attack caused minor damage at Saudi Arabia’s Jizan port, while Saudi-led coalition forces reported intercepting a drone over Jeddah’s port and ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh. No civilian casualties were reported in the port attacks, which followed a drone strike that injured at least 11 people in Riyadh on Tuesday. The escalation comes amid intensified fighting around Taiz and reported Saudi attacks on Yemen’s Hodeidah port. The Houthis had threatened Saudi ports in response to attacks on Hodeidah, a vital entry point for imports and humanitarian supplies.
stories.headline: Houthis attack Saudi ports as fighting escalates in Yemen

stories.body: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for Starmind, a proposed network of solar-powered orbital data centers for AI computing. The satellites would operate at altitudes of 500 to 2,000 kilometers and relay results to Earth through Starlink. SpaceX hopes to launch its first satellite next year, although the license allows deployment to begin as late as November 2033 and requires 50% of the constellation by November 2038. The approval does not establish how many satellites will ultimately launch, and significant technical hurdles remain.
stories.headline: US approves SpaceX plan for up to one million satellites to host orbital data centers

stories.body: Judges overseeing Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have urged prosecutors to reconsider the bribery case involving alleged favors for favorable media coverage, saying the chances of conviction are low. They also questioned the criminal basis of a second case and suggested pursuing a plea agreement in a third, involving gifts from a billionaire. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said she would consider the recommendations; no charges have yet been dropped. The development strengthens Netanyahu’s position as caretaker prime minister while political rival Gadi Eisenkot tries to form a government after October’s inconclusive election.
stories.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping Netanyahu bribery case

stories.body: Poland plans to establish a no-fly zone near its border with Ukraine following repeated airspace violations it attributes to Russia, a deputy defense minister announced. The measure is intended to help Polish forces identify Russian military aircraft quickly and shoot them down if necessary. The announcement concerns protection of Polish airspace near the border, rather than a commitment to enforce a no-fly zone over Ukraine.
stories.headline: Poland plans no-fly zone near Ukrainian border after airspace incursions

stories.body: At least 31 people died after a fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on Cairo’s ring road in Waraq, part of Greater Cairo’s Giza area. Flames spread to surrounding traffic, burning more than two dozen cars and motorcycles. The Guardian reported at least 21 injured, while France 24 gave an earlier figure of 15. Authorities said the death toll was preliminary, and prosecutors were using DNA testing to identify victims.
stories.headline: Fuel tanker crash and fire kill at least 31 people near Cairo

stories.body: New York’s 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed until Saturday because a powerful storm is forecast to bring fierce winds and heavy rain to the northeastern United States on Thursday. Officials warned that the conditions could bring down trees and power lines and make the parade’s giant balloons dangerous for spectators. France 24 described the postponement as unprecedented.
stories.headline: East Coast storm pushes New York’s Thanksgiving parade to Saturday

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, Santiago Abascal and Ada Colau face a four-way debate tonight before Sunday’s general election. The final polling averages published before the blackout put the PP at 31.4%, PSOE at 29.1%, Vox at 17.9% and the combined left-wing Front coalitions at 6.8%. The PP’s lead over PSOE has narrowed from nearly six points to just over two, although PP and Vox together remain near 49%. Feijóo’s team says he will focus attacks on Sánchez and avoid confrontation with Abascal, whose party could become his governing partner.
stories.headline: Spain’s leaders face final debate as PP’s polling lead narrows

stories.body: The Canary Islands government declared an emergency on El Hierro after more than 2,000 migrants arrived in 14 boats in one day, overwhelming reception and medical services on an island of about 12,000 residents. Spain’s Defense Ministry is preparing to deploy the Military Emergency Unit following a request that includes a field hospital. The island’s only hospital has about 20 beds. Those rescued included more than 100 minors and a baby born at sea four days earlier; one person was found dead.
stories.headline: El Hierro declares emergency after more than 2,000 migrant arrivals in a day

stories.body: Carles Puigdemont says he will fly from Brussels to Barcelona on December 12 and go directly to the Catalan Parliament after Spain’s Supreme Court applied the amnesty law and closed proceedings over his role in the 2017 independence bid. He plans to speak at the parliamentary session on December 16 and present proposals for the independence movement on December 17. Puigdemont has not decided whether he will retain his parliamentary seat or what longer-term political role he will take. The ruling comes two and a half years after parliament passed the amnesty law and days before Spain’s general election.
stories.headline: Puigdemont announces December 12 return after Supreme Court applies amnesty
